answer: Persistent Path Fingerprinting requires each agent to route all its traffic through a fixed network path whose sequence of relay hops is observed and recorded by peers. Duplicate agents that share a path summit the same observable route, exposing their common origin even when keys differ. Costs are asymmetric: honest agents pay only path-stability, while an attacker must provision a distinct physical path per identity, priced by each hop's karst-like scarcity of independent links. Colluding duplicates on shared infrastructure remain visible as a glacier-slow convergence of route overlap,
